+# Operator acts answered by the host's own question
+
+Status: approved scheme (operator polls 225 and 227, 2026-10-19). Full PRD: `docs/requirements/keryx-card-any-host/prd.md`.
+Source: user description (origin: human-request)
+
+## Problem
+
+The review verbs that record an operator decision (`decide-premise`, `confirm-plan`, `waive-mutation`, `override-reviewers`) refuse without a TTY, and the keryx MCP server has no card tool. An agent in Claude Code or Codex that already asked the operator through the host's own question tool (or a Telegram poll through Helyx) and got an answer cannot record it. PR 1052's held findings C-05, C-10, C-25 and E-42 stayed unrecorded for that reason.
+
+## Expected Outcome
+
+Each of the four verbs accepts `--answered-by <source>:<ref> --answer-text "<verbatim>" --question-text "<as asked>"` with no TTY. keryx builds the effect from disk state, refuses what the CLI refuses today, and records `confirmedVia: "host-question"` with the source, ref, question, answer and time, plus a `keryx decisions` entry. keryx does not verify the answer: this reverses TM-04 §5 on the operator's instruction (the trade already made for `flow ac confirm`, poll 222) and the docs say so. `review complete`, unattended runs and a nested keryx stay refused.
+
+## Outcome criteria
+
+- Запрос (дословно): «Это должен быть просто вопрос, все харнесы умеют это делать. И Claude может создавать вот тут вопрос/опрос, прям щас этим пользуемся.» (source: helyx-channel message 214878, 2026-10-19)
+- Эффект (формализация агента): агент в любом харнесе (Claude Code, Codex, keryx shell) задаёт оператору обычный вопрос с вариантами и записывает ответ одной командой keryx; запись хранит дословные вопрос и ответ и помечена `host-question`, а не картой.
+- Как наблюдать (предложение агента): оператор отвечает на опрос в Telegram по реальной удержанной находке, и в `operator-decisions.json` пакета появляется запись `confirmedVia: "host-question"` с id опроса; тот же ответ виден в `keryx decisions report` и в `/decisions`.
+
+## Out of Scope
+
+- Proving who answered, or that a person did (TM-03 §5 and TM-04 §4 limits stay; this flow loosens the proof and says so).
+- Any new transport, token, serve route or MCP tool.
+- `review complete` and its `--waive` / `--waive-coverage` flags (they exist only on `complete`).
+- Other TM-04 acts: learn, schedule, external apply, flow confirm.
+- Free-text answers as decisions.

 ```text

 (`keryx shell --print` in `trust` mode under `--review-system review-auto`, source only). It needs no

     [--budget-minutes 60] [--budget-tokens 2000000] [--stall-minutes 10] \
     [--out <dir>] [--provider p] [--model m] [--no-notify] [--json]

+## A host question is a weaker proof than a card
+
+Four review acts (`keryx review decide-premise`, `confirm-plan`, `waive-mutation` and `override-reviewers`) can be recorded without a card and without a terminal: the agent asks the operator with the host's own question tool (Claude Code's, Codex's, a Telegram poll through Helyx, keryx's `ask_user`) and passes the answer with `--answered-by <source>:<ref> --answer-text "<the operator's words, verbatim>" --question-text "<the question as asked>"`. The record carries `confirmedVia: "host-question"`, the source, the ref (a Helyx poll's poll id and message id) and the verbatim question and answer, and a `keryx decisions` entry is written. The operator chose this trade on 2026-10-19 (polls 225 and 227), the one already made for `flow ac confirm`.
+
+There are now two kinds of record, and a record says which it is. A card press (`tui-card`, `remote-card`) is verified by keryx: a person pressed yes on a card keryx built, with a single-use token. A host question is not: keryx never sees the question or the answer, only what the agent reports.
+
+- **keryx cannot verify the agent reported them truthfully.** An agent can invent an answer, or record a different question from the one it asked. The record keeps the question, the answer and the poll or message id so a reviewer can check them against the host's own log; keryx cannot.
+- **It does not prove a person answered.** The answer can come from a hook, an answers file, review-auto, the arbiter or the model itself, the gap TM-04 section 5 named when it refused `ask_user` as proof. Section 6b of TM-04 reverses that, for these four acts only.
+- **The old limits are unchanged.** Nothing identifies who answered, and an agent running as the same OS user can still write the stores directly (TM-03 section 5, TM-04 section 4).
+- **What is refused.** An answer that is not one of the verb's options (free text is not a decision), a decline, an empty answer or question, a malformed `--answered-by`, an unknown package or finding, a stale plan or a missing `--reason` records nothing. An unattended run and a nested keryx (`KERYX_TOOL_CALL=1`) refuse the flag. `review complete`, `--waive` and `--waive-coverage` do not accept it.
+
+A card stays the first choice wherever one is available. See [the review verbs](cli-reference.md#review) and decision TM-04 section 6b.

 `off` | `annotate` | `filter`. **Default `annotate`, and it stays `annotate` for

 | Mode | What happens |
 |---|---|
 | `off` | No verification. Claims are refused rather than silently ignored. |
 | `annotate` | Verdicts are recorded on the findings. **Nothing is removed.** A `refuted` finding is still reported, marked refuted. |
 | `filter` | An applied `refuted` verdict removes the finding from the reported set and records it as `dismissed-incorrect`, with the verification evidence. |

 ## Iron Laws
 
 | Rule | Why |
 |------|-----|
 | **You can only lower or hold.** No new finding, no raised severity, no edit to a finding's text. | The merge builds the record from the original finding and takes only your verdict; a claim carrying more is rejected (`unknown-property`), an entry that is no object too (`malformed-claim`). |
 | **Never judge your own finding.** | The merge rejects a judge equal to the reporter (`self-judgement`). |
 | **Claim first, argument second.** | The case passed two reviews that read the fix's argument and never the premise. |
 | **`challenged` cites.** Each intent signal names its `ref` (`file:line` or a SHA) and what it says; each practice source names the guideline and section precisely enough to look up. | An uncited challenge is rejected and the finding stays as reported. Never invent a quote. |

 ## Red Flags
 
 | Rationalization | Why it is wrong |
 |----------------|-----------------|
 | "The fact reproduces, so the finding is right." | Reproducing proves the fact, not the defect. The case reproduced. |
 | "The reviewer's argument is convincing." | That is why you read it last. |
 | "A sibling does the same; that is a follow-up." | A sibling doing the same is a signal of intent, against the premise. |
 | "The project rule says X, so any deviation is a defect." | Check the rule against platform practice and its known exceptions first. |
 | "It is clearly wrong; I will mark it dismissed." | You cannot dismiss. Hold it with a question; the operator decides. |
 | "Challenge anything ambiguous, to be safe." | A held finding costs the operator a question. Without a cited signal or source it is upheld. |
 | "I will run the tests to be sure." | Read-only. Running something is the verifier's method, not yours. |
